newsitem.title: JAPAN: Canadian bond dumping by Japan investors unlikely.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bond dumping by Japan investors unlikely.

text.p: Dumping of Canadian bonds by Japanese institutional investors does not appear to be behind recent sharp falls in those securities, despite overseas rumours to the contrary, fund managers and dealers here said.

A Tuesday Wall Street Journal report said there were U.S. market rumours that last week's Canadian bond slide may have been due to Japanese institutional investors dumping as much as $1 billion in Canadian bonds.
Managers here disagreed. "I don't believe such large sales would emerge all at once," said Shinji Koma, a manager at the international department of Asahi Mutual Life Insurance.
He added: "If there were sales, at least it wasn't us selling." Asahi Mutual is the largest holder of Canadian assets among Japan's eight major life insurance companies.

Although Koma acknowledged that upward momentum in Canadian bonds has been slowing, he said improved economic fundamentals in Canada and the still-large interest rate gap with Japan meant Japanese investors were in no hurry to sell right now.

He and other fund managers added that, while there may well have been some sales by Japanese investors seeking to take profits, U.S. and European operators appear to have been by far the most active sellers as they, too, looked for profits.

A manager at another major life insurer with large Canadian holdings agreed. "Even if Canadian bonds decline a bit, comparable interest rates in Japan are still so low that investors will still hang onto high-yielders like these."
He said that some sales may have emerged from Japanese banks interested in shifting short-term Canadian assets into longer-term investments, not necessarily in Canadian dollars.

A dealer with a Canadian bank in Tokyo said even though the Canadian dollar has been declining a bit, this was mainly due to position adjustments and was not serious enough to force Japanese investors into dumping Canadian assets.
Asahi Mutual's Koma agreed. "We are still comfortable with the currency's performance," he said.
The Canadian dollar was around 82.82/92 yen in late Tokyo compared with 82.98 yen at the close of Tuesday's Canadian trade.
